solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Housing situation experienced by actors on film?

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece written on another follows it, so the union comes after the film

parts.note: a photographic film once developed is a negative
Equity is the British actors' trade union

explanation.surface: A wry question about what actors go through when filming.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the actors' union in Britain. Negative equity is when a home is worth less than the mortgage on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Negative equity is a predicament in the property market where a mortgage exceeds the home's value.

clue.text: Not working after present discharge

indicators.note: the off part comes after the give part in the answer

parts.note: to present is to give
a machine that is off is not working

explanation.surface: Someone released from work after a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To give off fumes is to discharge or emit them, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Name given to salt lake

indicators.note: given to means added onto, so the name's letter is attached after the sailor

parts.note: a salt or a tar is an old sailor

explanation.surface: A salt lake being given its name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt lake' looks like one phrase; 'salt' is the sailor and 'lake' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, especially in northern England.

clue.text: Plant cover in a mess

indicators.note: the words 'in a mess' tell us the preceding letters are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A plant cover left in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mess' signals the anagram, but 'in' and 'a' are also part of the fodder: COVER IN A rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica, or speedwell, is a flowering garden plant genus.

clue.text: Journalist has to pull up King

parts.note: ED, an editor, is the crossword journalist

indicators.note: in a down answer, 'up' means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: A journalist told to rein in a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist; in a down clue 'up' signals writing a word bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward is the name of several English kings, so a king is an example.

clue.text: Winning team gets depressed in confusion

parts.note: a side that is up is ahead or winning
a side is a team
down means depressed

explanation.surface: A victorious team somehow ends up feeling low and muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: A room turned upside down is in total disorder, an idiom for confusion.

clue.text: Negative feedback on mostly divine languages

indicators.note: feeding back sends the word the other way, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: not is a negative

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to divine is to guess

explanation.surface: Critical comments on a nearly holy tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feedback' turns NOT into TON; 'mostly' cuts GUESS to GUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongues is an old and biblical word for languages, as in speaking in tongues.

clue.text: Wanting to join part needed in series

parts.note: wanting means lacking or missing
to link is to join

explanation.surface: A craftsman lacking the piece needed to complete a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A missing link is the absent element that would complete a sequence or chain.

clue.text: How one obtains funds from extra lottery?

parts.note: an extra in cricket can be likened to an over, something beyond
a lottery is a draw

explanation.surface: A question about winning money in a bonus lottery.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is whimsical: overdrawing is a way of getting money out of the bank beyond what you hold.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdraw an account is to withdraw more money than it contains, a way of obtaining funds.

clue.text: Evil individual seen crossing a peninsula

indicators.note: crossing here means stretching across, so the pieces go either side of the letter a

parts.note: sin is evil
I is one, an individual

explanation.surface: A wicked person spotted travelling across a peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts A between SIN and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinai is the Egyptian peninsula between the Gulf of Suez and the Gulf of Aqaba.

clue.text: All steroids may be incompatible

indicators.note: 'may be' suggests the letters could be made into something else by rearranging

explanation.surface: A warning that some steroids may clash with each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Things ill-assorted are badly matched and do not go together, so they are incompatible.

clue.text: Closed circuit look at work

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
op, an operation, is a piece of work

explanation.surface: Someone checking a CCTV system at the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a closed path or circuit, a synonym in electronics.

clue.text: They're beaten if caught with shorts

parts.note: snared means caught in a trap
shorts are spirits served in small measures, such as rums

explanation.surface: People punished for being caught wearing shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'shorts' are spirits, as opposed to long drinks like beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Snare drums are struck with sticks, so they are things that get beaten.

clue.text: Ways of speaking about spinner's production

definitions.meaning: a speaker's delivery is their manner of speaking
in cricket a spin bowler produces balls bowled, each one a delivery

explanation.surface: A remark on the speech habits of a cricket spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket each ball bowled is a delivery; a spinner is a slow bowler who spins the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliveries are both styles of speaking and balls bowled by a cricketer.

clue.text: A source of light forces change outside

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter
change tells us the letters of the word forces are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lamp's beam is changed by outside forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco means in the open air, so it means outside.

clue.text: The chances of success for unusual issue

parts.note: odd means unusual
a son is a child, one's issue

explanation.surface: Betting on how a strange child will turn out.
explanation.walkthrough: Odds-on describes a bet where success is more likely than failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds-on describes good betting chances, where success is more likely than not.

clue.text: Make light of attractive girl taking in dress

indicators.note: taking in means containing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
a mini is a short dress

explanation.surface: A pretty girl having a dress altered, laughing it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make light of' looks like an idiom for joking; here it means lessen.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish something is to belittle it, playing down its importance.

clue.text: Interference caused by a nervous reaction on the way

parts.note: St, street, is a way
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A driver blaming a crackling radio for a twitch on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Static is crackling electrical interference on a radio or phone line.

clue.text: A student right to accept endless cash from old social worker

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the money goes inside the other letters

parts.note: L for learner, a student driver

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: money is cash

explanation.surface: A student accepting cash from a social worker of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: An almoner was a British hospital social worker; the title fell out of use, hence 'old'. 'to accept' and 'endless' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: An almoner was a hospital social worker, a now-obsolete title in Britain.

clue.text: Fair offer for a round trip

definitions.text: Fair offer for a round trip

parts.words: Fair offer for a round trip
parts.note: read 'fair' as a funfair, and the offer is a ride that goes around in a circle

explanation.surface: A reasonable deal on a return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like an adjective meaning reasonable, but it is a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: A big wheel is a fairground ride carrying passengers round in a huge vertical circle.

clue.text: Former coastal towns generating contributions towards balance of trade

parts.note: ex means former
ports are coastal towns

explanation.surface: Old harbours producing goods for the national trade figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Exports are goods sold abroad, which count on one side of a country's trade balance.

clue.text: One's interest is from certain investment in an old city

indicators.note: investing in, like putting money in, means placing the word inside another

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone who earns interest from a safe investment in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword regular; 'investment in' plays on money while signalling a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer is a moneylender charging interest, the person whose income it is.

clue.text: Tourism rep's new outfit for play

indicators.note: new tells us to make a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A holiday rep's new outfit for leisure time.
explanation.definitionFit: A romper suit is a one-piece garment worn by young children for playing in.

clue.text: Unrestricted circular enclosure

parts.note: O is a circular letter
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: A round pen with no fence restrictions.
explanation.definitionFit: Open means free of limits or barriers, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sort of colonnade to put in South America

indicators.note: put in means placed inside another word

explanation.surface: Instructions to build a colonnade in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a classical Greek covered walkway with columns, a type of colonnade.

clue.text: Feeling surrounded by drunken nuisances

indicators.note: the letters are enclosed within the words drunken nuisances, running across both

explanation.surface: How it feels to be surrounded by drunks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a feeling of weary boredom and dissatisfaction.

clue.text: Revels at seeing one in duty lists

indicators.note: in means one is placed inside the duty lists

parts.note: rosters are lists of who is on duty
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone celebrating on finding themselves on the rota.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily, so roisters means revels as a verb.

clue.text: Share deals? Errs badly in practice

indicators.note: badly tells us the letters are to be put in disarray

explanation.surface: Stock trading mistakes made badly during a training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges SHARE DEALS and ERRS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress rehearsal is the final practice of a show in full costume.
